2608.25881.title: Loss-Based Active Learning for Neural Abstractive Summarization
2608.25881.paper_summary: Fine-tuning abstractive summarization models requires high-quality annotated data. However, obtaining such corpora is expensive and time-consuming, as it requires human annotators to read and comprehend long documents to create accurate summaries. Active learning mitigates this issue by selecting only the most informative instances for annotation, allowing models to achieve competitive results with significantly fewer labels. However, the application of active learning to summarization remains under-explored, and existing studies often suffer from instability and significant computational bottlenecks. To overcome these challenges, we propose LOBSTER (LOss-BaSed acTivE leaRning), a novel active learning framework designed specifically for abstractive summarization. LOBSTER improves performance by prioritizing unlabeled instances semantically similar to the model's current high-loss training examples, enabling the model to explicitly correct its specific weaknesses. Our empirical evaluation across three benchmark datasets and two summarization backbone models demonstrates that LOBSTER consistently matches or outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches while achieving a query selection speedup of up to 665x.
2608.25881.paper_summary_zh: 精調抽象摘要模型需要高品質的標註數據。<lb/>然而，獲得這樣的語料庫既昂貴又耗時，因為這需要人工標註者閱讀和理解長篇文件以創建準確的摘要。<lb/>主動學習通過僅選擇最具信息量的實例進行標註來緩解這一問題，使模型能夠以顯著更少的標籤達到競爭性的結果。<lb/>然而，主動學習在摘要中的應用仍然未被充分探索，現有研究往往存在不穩定性和顯著的計算瓶頸。<lb/>為了克服這些挑戰，我們提出了LOBSTER（LOss-BaSed acTivE leaRning），這是一個專門為抽象摘要設計的新型主動學習框架。<lb/>LOBSTER通過優先考慮與模型當前高損失訓練示例語義相似的未標註實例來提高性能，使模型能夠明確地糾正其特定的弱點。<lb/>我們在三個基準數據集和兩個摘要主幹模型上的實證評估表明，LOBSTER始終能夠與當前最先進的方法相匹配或超越，同時實現高達665倍的查詢選擇加速。
